newsitem.title: ISRAEL: CPI not seen greatly affecting Israel market.
newsitem.headline: CPI not seen greatly affecting Israel market.

text.p: Israeli traders welcomed on Tuesday the low 0.4 percent rise in September's consumer price index but said it was unlikely to have much affect on the stock market.
Boaz Leviatan, an analyst at Sahar Securities: "Recently the market has been politically driven even though there is a fairly wide concensus that the market is fundamentally cheap."
He said he did not believe inflation or prospects for an interest rate cut would significantly affect share prices.
Ronen Kaufman of Nesuah Trading said: "This was a strong positive sign among much negative data in the recent period, but you can't read too much into one CPI."
He said it was unclear whether this was a real turnaround in inflation. The market now will wait to see what the central bank will do with interest rates at the end of the month.
Yakov Sheinin, head of Economic Models consultants, told Israel Radio that forecasts had called for a low CPI of about 0.5 percent.
"We think the inflation rate will accelerate in the coming months," Sheinin said, adding he feared Israel would face an economic slowdown coupled with annual inflation of about 12 percent.
Dan Propper, head of the Manufacturers Association, called for a reduction in interest rates to boost economic growth and "pull the exports sector out of the mud it is now in".
Danny Gillerman, head of the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce, called for an interest rate cut of at least two percentage points.
"This won't bring about an acceleration in inflation but certainly will prevent the economy from slipping into a deep recession," he said in a statement.
Gillerman said the low CPI increases of recent months, while positive, indicate a slowdown was overtaking the economy.
